epithet: al-Kubra (the Great); Sayyidat Nisa al-Alamin (Leader of the Women of the Worlds)
tribe: Quraysh - Banu Asad ibn Abd al-Uzzah

Mother of all the Prophet's surviving children
summary: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (RA) was the first wife of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the first person — male or female — to believe in the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ. A respected and wealthy businesswoman of Makkah, she was the Prophet's companion, supporter, and anchor through the most difficult years of the early Makkan period, and her death was one of the greatest personal griefs of the Prophet's life.
biography:
Khadijah bint Khuwaylid ibn Asad al-Qurashiyyah was born around 555 CE in Makkah into the Banu Asad clan of Quraysh, a clan of high standing in Makkan society. She was the daughter of Khuwaylid ibn Asad, a respected merchant and warrior, and her mother was Fatimah bint Za'idah. She was given the epithet al-Tahirah (the Pure One) by the Quraysh in recognition of her character and nobility of conduct even before the coming of Islam.

Khadijah was widowed twice before her marriage to the Prophet ﷺ and had become, through her own acumen and force of character, a successful and independent merchant. She employed men to manage trade caravans on her behalf, paying them from her own capital and receiving a share of the profits. It was in this capacity that she first encountered Muhammad ibn Abdullah ﷺ, who was then around twenty-five years old and had earned the reputation among all of Quraysh as al-Amin (the Trustworthy). She hired him to lead a trading caravan to Syria, sending her servant Maysarah along to observe him.

Maysarah's report upon their return was extraordinary: Muhammad ﷺ had been more honest, more capable, and more remarkable than anyone she had ever employed. Khadijah had also received an account — which varies in classical sources — of certain signs Maysarah observed during the journey that pointed toward his special status. She proposed marriage to him through an intermediary. The Prophet ﷺ agreed; they married around 595 CE when he was approximately twenty-five and she was approximately forty years old, though some classical scholars record slightly different ages. (Ibn Hisham, al-Seerah al-Nabawiyyah; Ibn Sa'd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, Vol. 8)

For fifteen years before the first revelation, they lived in a deeply devoted marriage. Khadijah bore him six children: al-Qasim (who died in infancy), Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, Fatimah al-Zahra, and Abdullah (also known as al-Tayyib and al-Tahir, who also died in infancy). Fatimah al-Zahra (RA) alone survived the Prophet ﷺ, albeit only briefly. From Fatimah's marriage to Ali ibn Abi Talib descends all prophetic lineage.

When revelation first came to the Prophet ﷺ in the Cave of Hira — around 610 CE — and he returned home trembling, overwhelmed, and saying 'Cover me! Cover me!' (Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab Bad' al-Wahy), it was Khadijah who enveloped him in a cloak and calmed him with words of profound wisdom and faith: 'By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You uphold family ties, you carry the burden of the weak, you give to those who have nothing, you serve your guests generously, and you assist those afflicted by hardship.' She then took him to her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal, a scholar of the earlier scriptures, who confirmed that what had come to Muhammad ﷺ was the same divine revelation (al-Namus) that had come to Moses.

Khadijah was, without qualification, the first Muslim — the first person in history to affirm the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ and accept the faith of Islam. She believed without hesitation, in the moment of his greatest uncertainty. Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim both record this, and there is no scholarly dispute on this point. She spent her entire wealth in the service of Islam and the protection of the early Muslim community, donating to the poor, supporting the persecuted, and providing the Prophet ﷺ with the material security that allowed him to devote himself to his mission.

During the Makkan years, when the Banu Hashim and Banu Muttalib were subject to a three-year social and economic boycott imposed by Quraysh, Khadijah endured the boycott alongside the Prophet ﷺ in Shi'b Abi Talib — a mountain pass outside Makkah where the besieged community lived in deprivation. The boycott broke her health significantly.

Khadijah died in 10 Nabawi (approximately 619 CE), just three years before the Hijrah — before she could see the triumph of the faith she had supported from its very first moment. The year of her death, alongside the death of Abu Talib, is known in the Seerah as 'the Year of Sorrow' ('Am al-Huzn). The Prophet ﷺ was deeply affected by her loss and spoke of her with love and gratitude for the rest of his life.

The Prophet ﷺ said of her: 'She believed in me when people disbelieved in me. She trusted me when people denied me. She supported me with her wealth when people withheld from me. And Allah gave me children through her while withholding them from the other wives.' (Musnad Ahmad, authenticated; similar narration in Sahih Muslim). Jibril (AS) came to the Prophet ﷺ on one occasion and said: 'Tell Khadijah that her Lord gives her greetings of peace, and gives her glad tidings of a house in Paradise made of brocade, in which there is neither noise nor fatigue.' (Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab Fada'il Ashab al-Nabi; Sahih Muslim).

She was given the title 'Sayyidat Nisa al-Alamin' (Leader of the Women of the Worlds) in classical hadith narrations alongside Fatimah, Maryam bint Imran, and Asiyah bint Muzahim. Her station in Islam — as the first believer, the Prophet's most devoted supporter, and the mother of his surviving legacy — is beyond comparison. All Sunni scholars are unanimous in her extraordinary rank.

First person to accept Islam when revelation descended on the Prophet ﷺ
Endured the Quraysh boycott of Banu Hashim in Shi'b Abi Talib
Died in Makkah; Year of Sorrow ('Am al-Huzn)

notable_traits: First Muslim — the first person to affirm the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ
Complete financial generosity — donated all her wealth to the Islamic cause
Wisdom and emotional intelligence — her words of comfort at the first revelation steadied the Prophet ﷺ
Exceptional businesswoman and community figure in pre-Islamic Makkah
Deep, unwavering loyalty to the Prophet ﷺ throughout his life
